_why: Each mutation is a way a hand-rolled anchored substitution already fails. The first two are the original silent no-op the helper was filed against: an anchor assert that stops refusing writes into the wrong place or not at all. The rest strip one refusal each. The accept case is NOT tested here -- a guard that refuses everything kills every mutant -- it is pinned by TestAccepts in the suite, which these mutants must leave passing.

mutations.name: missing-anchor-becomes-a-silent-noop
mutations._mechanism: The original defect: a drifted anchor writes nothing and reports success. Must be caught by test_a_missing_section_refuses, NOT merely by a crash.

mutations.name: two-anchors-take-the-first
mutations._mechanism: What `.replace()` does natively: silently picks match 1. Caught by test_two_headers_refuse_rather_than_taking_the_first.

mutations.name: loosen-the-anchor-to-ignore-indentation
mutations._mechanism: A stripped-line anchor finds the 7 fenced template examples in references/inline-protocols.md and refuses a doc that is not ambiguous. This is the exact mismatch that a stripped corpus measurement hid.

mutations.name: reformat-tables-instead-of-refusing
mutations._mechanism: Mangles a 140-section shape into a bullet list. Caught by test_a_table_section_refuses_rather_than_being_reformatted.

mutations.name: guess-placement-on-an-unsorted-section
mutations._mechanism: The 22%-wrong case. Appending blind to a 1.0/1.2/1.1 section is wrong in a way no assertion on the write itself sees.

mutations.name: descending-sections-get-appended-at-the-end
mutations._mechanism: Placement derived but then ignored -- the entry lands at the bottom of a newest-first log. Must be caught by test_descending_section_gets_the_entry_at_the_top, not by any refusal test.

mutations.name: allow-the-same-version-twice
mutations._mechanism: 27 bumps per session means re-runs happen; the anchor still matches on the second run, so a substitution appends a duplicate.

mutations.name: compare-versions-as-strings
mutations._mechanism: v1.10 < v1.9 lexically, so a correctly ascending section reads as unsorted and is refused. Caught by test_ten_sorts_after_nine_not_before -- a false-POSITIVE guard, the direction mutation testing usually misses.

mutations.name: accept-a-multiline-entry-body
mutations._mechanism: A newline in --text smuggles a second list item past every other check.

mutations.name: stop-at-headers-but-not-at-rules
mutations._mechanism: 20 of 713 sections end at `---`. Without the rule terminator the append lands below it, in the next section's prose.
mutations.find: while end < len(lines) and not HEADER.match(lines[end]) and not RULE.match(lines[end]):
mutations.replace: while end < len(lines) and not HEADER.match(lines[end]):

mutations.name: refusal-line-carries-a-line-number
mutations._mechanism: Makes a cannot-write readable as a write that landed -- the cannot-judge-carries-no-count invariant.

mutations.name: refusal-exits-zero
mutations._mechanism: An `&&`-chained audit loop would proceed past a doc that never got bumped.

mutations.name: dry-run-writes-anyway
mutations._mechanism: A preflight that mutates the tree it is previewing.

mutations.name: splice-self-check-never-fires
mutations._mechanism: The insertion-only assert is the last line of defence against a slice that ate a neighbour. Expected to be caught by the untouched-document test rather than by a dedicated one.
